claim: A combination of three transcription factors, Ngn3, Mafa, and Pdx1, directly reprograms pancreatic acinar cells to β-cells.
source: We previously reported that a combination of three transcription factors, Ngn3, Mafa, and Pdx1, directly reprograms pancreatic acinar cells to β-cells.
evidence: This is a statement of prior work by the authors, supported by citation to their previous publication.

claim: Acinar cells can be converted to δ-like cells by Ngn3.
source: We now show that acinar cells can be converted to δ-like and α-like cells by Ngn3 and Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1-2.

claim: Acinar cells can be converted to α-like cells by Ngn3+Mafa.
source: We now show that acinar cells can be converted to δ-like and α-like cells by Ngn3 and Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript, supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: Three major islet endocrine subtypes can be derived by acinar reprogramming.
source: Thus, three major islet endocrine subtypes can be derived by acinar reprogramming.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experimental data showing conversion to β-, δ-, and α-cells.

claim: Ngn3 promotes establishment of a generic endocrine state in acinar cells.
source: Ngn3 promotes establishment of a generic endocrine state in acinar cells, and also promotes δ-specification in the absence of other factors.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5 showing Ngn3 suppresses acinar factors and activates pan-endocrine genes.

claim: Ngn3 promotes δ-specification in the absence of other factors.
source: Ngn3 promotes establishment of a generic endocrine state in acinar cells, and also promotes δ-specification in the absence of other factors.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Ngn3 alone induces somatostatin+ cells (Figures 1-2).

claim: δ-specification is suppressed by Mafa and Pdx1 during α- and β-cell induction.
source: δ-specification is in turn suppressed by Mafa and Pdx1 during α- and β-cell induction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 9 showing reduced somatostatin induction when Mafa or Pdx1 are co-expressed with Ngn3.

claim: The pancreatic islets contain three major hormone-secreting endocrine subtypes: insulin+ β-cells, glucagon+ α-cells, and somatostatin+ δ-cells.
source: The pancreatic islets contain three major hormone-secreting endocrine subtypes: insulin + β-cells, glucagon + α-cells, and somatostatin + δ-cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pancreatic islet composition.

claim: Expression of Ngn3 alone induced 40 ± 3% of the infected mCherry+ cells to become somatostatin+.
source: Expression of Ngn3 alone induced 40 ± 3% of the infected mCherry+ cells to become somatostatin+ (Sst).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experiments shown in Figure 1B-D with statistical measurements.

claim: Co-infection of two separate viruses carrying Ngn3 and Mafa resulted in the formation of both glucagon+ and somatostatin+ cells in 11 ± 6% and 9 ± 5% of infected cells, respectively.
source: Co-infection of two separate viruses carrying Ngn3 and Mafa resulted in the formation of both glucagon+ (Gcg) and somatostatin+ cells in 11 ± 6% and 9 ± 5% of infected cells, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experiments shown in Figure 1E-G with statistical measurements.

claim: Co-expression of Ngn3, Mafa, Pdx1, and mCherry from a single polycistronic construct led to exclusive formation of insulin+ cells in 47 ± 8% of the mCherry+ cells.
source: Co-expression of Ngn3, Mafa, Pdx1, and mCherry from a single polycistronic construct led to exclusive formation of insulin+ cells in 47 ± 8% of the mCherry+ cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experiments shown in Figure 1H-I with statistical measurements.

claim: Induced δ-cells co-express somatostatin and cholecystokinin receptor B (Cckbr).
source: Induced δ-cells co-express somatostatin (SST) and cholecystokinin receptor B (Cckbr) (A and A′).
evidence: This is shown by immunostaining data in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Induced δ-cells co-express the endocrine markers Pax6 and Synaptophysin.
source: They also co-express the endocrine markers Pax6 (B and B′) and Synaptophysin (Syn, C and C′).
evidence: This is shown by immunostaining data in Figure 2B-C.

claim: The secretory granules of induced δ-cells are spherical or ellipsoidal with matrix filling the entire granule space.
source: Electron microscopy analysis revealed that the secretory granules of induced δ-cells are spherical or ellipsoidal with matrix filling the entire granule space (Figure 2E,E′).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2E,E'.

claim: The morphology of induced δ-cell granules is typical of endogenous δ-cells and distinct from that of α-or β-granules.
source: This morphology is typical of endogenous δ-cells (Figure 2D,D′) and distinct from that of α-or β-granules (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on comparative electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 2D-E and supplement 2.

claim: Induced δ-cells were embedded among acinar cells.
source: In addition, we observed that the induced δ-cells were embedded among acinar cells (Figure 2E, arrow points to dense assembly of endoplasmic reticulum in a neighboring acinar cell).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Endogenous δ-cells reside exclusively within islets.
source: In contrast, endogenous δ-cells reside exclusively within islets (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 2D and is established knowledge.

claim: Gene profiling yielded 1283 genes enriched in the induced δ-cells relative to acinar cells.
source: Gene profiling with illumina arrays yielded 1283 genes enriched in the induced δ-cells (30 days after induction) relative to acinar cells (GEO: GSE52522).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from gene expression profiling experiments.

claim: 632 of the induced genes (49%) overlapped with the islet-enriched gene set.
source: 632 of the induced genes (49%) overlapped with the islet-enriched gene set that we previously reported (Figure 2F) (Zhou et al., 2008) (GEO: GSE12025).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparative gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: δ-cells represent 5.5% of total mouse islet cells as determined by FACS.
source: Given that δ-cells represent a minor fraction of total mouse islet cells (5.5% as determined by FACS, see Figure 2—figure supplement 4)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from FACS analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Up-regulation of Hhex was detected in induced δ-cells.
source: We detected up-regulation of Hhex (Figure 2G), a gene recently implicated in δ-cell biology (72nd ADA abstract, Klaus Kaestner lab).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 2G and cited work.

claim: Glucagon, insulin, and the β-cell marker Nkx6.1 are abundantly expressed in islets but absent from induced δ-cells.
source: In contrast, glucagon, insulin, and the β-cell marker Nkx6.1 are abundantly expressed in islets but absent from induced δ-cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: None of the CpG sites assayed in the somatostatin promoters was methylated in all samples tested.
source: None of the CpG sites assayed in the somatostatin promoters was methylated in all samples tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), indicating that this promoter is not subject to regulation by DNA methylation.
evidence: This is based on DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Amylase2 was largely unmethylated in acinar cells.
source: Amylase2, a gene exclusively expressed in pancreatic acinar cells, was largely unmethylated in acinar cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is based on DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The induced δ-cells showed strong methylation in the Amylase2 promoter similar to islet δ-cells.
source: In contrast, the induced δ-cells showed strong methylation in this promoter similar to islet δ-cells (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is based on DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H and supplement 6.

claim: The Insulin2 promoter was fully methylated in acinar cells but partially demethylated in both endogenous and induced δ-cells.
source: The Insulin2 promoter was fully methylated in acinar cells but partially demethylated in both endogenous and induced δ-cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is based on DNA methylation analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The methylation differences of acinar/islet δ-cell and acinar/induced δ-cell are statistically highly significant (p<0.001) for both amylase and Insulin promoters.
source: For both amylase and Insulin promoters, the methylation differences of acinar/islet δ-cell and acinar/induced δ-cell are statistically highly significant (p<0.001)
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the DNA methylation data.

claim: There is no significant difference between islet δ-cells and induced δ-cells in DNA methylation (p=0.23 and 0.30 for amylase and insulin promoter respectively).
source: whereas there is no significant difference between islet δ-cells and induced δ-cells (p=0.23 and 0.30 for amylase and insulin promoter respectively).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the DNA methylation data.

claim: Substantial DNA methylation changes occurred during acinar to δ-cell conversion in the promoters studied.
source: These studies suggest that substantial DNA methylation changes occurred during acinar to δ-cell conversion in the promoters we studied.
evidence: This is an inference based on the DNA methylation data presented.

claim: The induced δ-cells responded to Arginine and released somatostatin, in a manner similar to isolated islets which contain endogenous δ-cells.
source: The induced δ-cells responded to Arginine and released somatostatin, in a manner similar to isolated islets which contain endogenous δ-cells (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is based on in vitro hormone secretion assay data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Control acinar cells did not respond to Arginine stimulation.
source: In contrast, control acinar cells did not respond to Arginine stimulation (Figure 2I), consistent with the fact that they do not express endocrine hormones.
evidence: This is based on in vitro hormone secretion assay data shown in Figure 2I and established knowledge.

claim: Induced δ-cells possess cellular machineries necessary for hormone production, storage, and release.
source: These data suggest that induced δ-cells possess cellular machineries necessary for hormone production, storage, and release.
evidence: This is an inference based on the hormone secretion assay results.

claim: δ-like cells induced by Ngn3 expression in adult pancreas possess key features of endogenous δ-cells.
source: The data described above collectively indicate that δ-like cells induced by Ngn3 expression in adult pancreas possess key features of endogenous δ-cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in Figures 1-2.

claim: All induced Gcg+ cells expressed strong Arx expression.
source: We observed strong Arx expression in all induced Gcg+ cells, although some Gcg− cells also expressed Arx (Figures 3B,B′).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B,B'.

claim: All Gcg+ cells expressed the endocrine genes Pax6 and synaptophysin.
source: In addition, all Gcg+ cells expressed the endocrine genes Pax6 (Figure 3C,C′) and synaptophysin (Figure 3D,D′).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: The secretory granules of induced α-cells have a narrow halo between the core and membrane that is typical of α-granules and distinct from δ- and β-granules.
source: The secretory granules have a narrow halo between the core and membrane (Figure 3E′,F′) that is typical of α-granules and distinct from δ- and β-granules (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 3E',F' and supplement 2.

claim: The induced α-like cells were intermingled among acinar cells.
source: The induced α-like cells were intermingled among acinar cells (Figure 3F, arrow points to zymogene granules of a neighboring acinar cells)
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Endogenous α-cells were found exclusively within islets.
source: whereas endogenous α-cells were found exclusively within islets (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 3E and is established knowledge.

claim: The acinar fraction that contains induced α-cells responded to the secretagogue Arginine and released glucagon.
source: In an in vitro hormone secretion assay, the acinar fraction that contains induced α-cells isolated from the adult pancreas 30 days after induction responded to the secretagogue Arginine and released glucagon (Figure 3H)
evidence: This is based on in vitro hormone secretion assay data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Statistical analysis showed no significant difference between endogenous and induced α-cells at glucagon and insulin promoters (p=0.26, 0.50, respectively).
source: Statistical analysis showed no significant difference between endogenous and induced cells at glucagon and insulin promoters (p=0.26, 0.50, respectively).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: A difference in DNA methylation was detected at the amylase promoter between endogenous and induced α-cells (p=0.02).
source: However, a difference was detected at the amylase promoter (p=0.02).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of DNA methylation data.

claim: Amylase protein expression was absent in the majority of Gcg+ cells (over 95%).
source: Amylase protein expression was absent in the majority of Gcg+ cells (over 95%).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining quantification.

claim: A small fraction (<5% of all Gcg+ cells) were Amylase+, indicating incomplete reprogramming in a small subset of glucagon+ cells.
source: However, a small fraction (<5% of all Gcg+ cells) were Amylase+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 4), indicating incomplete reprogramming in a small subset of glucagon+ cells.
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Induced α-cells possess key features of endogenous α-cells.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that induced α-cells possess key features of endogenous α-cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in Figure 3.

claim: Tamoxifen induction of bigenic Ptf1aCreER::RosaYFP animals led to specific and indelible labeling of approximately 20% of adult pancreatic acinar cells.
source: Tamoxifen induction of bigenic Ptf1aCreER::RosaYFP animals led to specific and indelible labeling of approximately 20% of adult pancreatic acinar cells.
evidence: This is based on genetic lineage tracing experiments.

claim: Delivery of Ngn3+Mafa or Ngn3 by adenovirus in the pancreas resulted in formation of Gcg+YFP+Cherry+ and Sst+YFP+Cherry+ cells, indicating that the induced cells derive from adult acinar cells.
source: Delivery of Ngn3+Mafa or Ngn3 by adenovirus in the pancreas resulted in formation of Gcg+YFP+Cherry+ (A–A′′, arrows) and Sst+YFP+Cherry+ (B–B′′, arrows) cells, indicating that the induced cells derive from adult acinar cells.
evidence: This is based on genetic lineage tracing data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Only about 1% of the induced δ- and α-cells incorporated BrdU in a 10-day reprogramming period.
source: Only about 1% of the induced δ- and α-cells incorporated BrdU in a 10-day reprogramming period (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on BrdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 4C-E.

claim: The conversion of acinar cells to induced δ- and α-cells occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation.
source: Continuous BrdU labeling showed that the conversion of acinar cells to induced δ- and α-cells occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on BrdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 4C-D and is an inference from the low BrdU incorporation.

claim: Induced δ- and α-cells derive from adult acinar cells.
source: These studies confirmed that induced δ- and α-cells derive from adult acinar cells and that the acinar conversion occurred largely in the absence of cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on lineage tracing and BrdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 are key acinar cell-fate regulators.
source: Ptf1a, Nr5a2, and Mist1 are key acinar cell-fate regulators. They are expressed in adult acinar; their genetic deletion results in abnormalities of acinar development and function
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Ngn3 and Mafa, but not Pdx1, strongly suppressed the expression of the acinar fate-regulators Mist1, Ptf1a, and Nr5a2 4 days after expression in the pancreas.
source: Immunohistochemistry showed that 4 days after expression of the three reprogramming factors individually in the pancreas, Ngn3 and Mafa, but not Pdx1, strongly suppressed the expression of the acinar fate-regulators Mist1, Ptf1a, and Nr5a2 (A, B, E, F, I, J, M).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A,B,E,F,I,J,M.

claim: Ngn3 activated expression of the pan-endocrine genes Pax6 and Islet1, whereas Mafa and Pdx1 did not.
source: Ngn3 also activated expression of the pan-endocrine genes Pax6 and Islet1 (C, D, M), whereas Mafa and Pdx1 did not (G, H, K, L, M).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5C,D,G,H,K,L,M.

claim: Ngn3 alone can establish an endocrine state in acinar cells by simultaneous suppression of acinar factors and activation of pan-endocrine genes.
source: Ngn3 alone can therefore establish an endocrine state in acinar cells by simultaneous suppression of acinar factors and activation of pan-endocrine genes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing Ngn3 suppresses acinar factors and activates pan-endocrine genes.

claim: Pax6 and Islet1 are endocrine genes expressed in all islet endocrine cells.
source: Pax6 and Islet1 are endocrine genes expressed in all islet endocrine cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pancreatic endocrine cells.

claim: Genetic studies have established the important role of Pax6 and Islet1 in the development of all islet endocrine subtypes.
source: Genetic studies have established their important role in the development of all islet endocrine subtypes (Ahlgren et al., 1997; Sander et al., 1997; Ashery-Padan et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Among the three reprogramming factors, Ngn3 alone possesses the ability to initiate two key events in endocrine reprogramming: acinar suppression and pan-endocrine activation.
source: The data discussed above together indicate that among the three reprogramming factors, Ngn3 alone possesses the ability to initiate two key events in endocrine reprogramming, namely, acinar suppression and pan-endocrine activation, thereby establishing a generic endocrine state in acinar cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Co-expression of Nr5a2 and Ngn3 strongly inhibited the activation of both Pax6 and Sst compared with Ngn3 alone.
source: Compared with the robust induction of Pax6 and Sst by Ngn3 alone (A, D, G), co-expression of Nr5a2 and Ngn3 (by co-infection of two separate viruses) strongly inhibited the activation of both endocrine genes (B, E, G).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A,B,D,E,G.

claim: A similar suppression of Pax6 and Sst was observed when Ngn3 was co-expressed with Ptf1a.
source: A similar suppression was observed when Ngn3 was co-expressed with Ptf1a (C, F, G).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6C,F,G.

claim: Key acinar factors act as molecular barriers in endocrine conversion.
source: Given the important role played by key acinar factors in maintaining acinar cell fate, we hypothesized that these factors could act as molecular barriers in endocrine conversion. We tested this hypothesis by co-infecting pancreas with two viruses carrying
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested and supported by the data in Figure 6.

claim: Strong suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 was observed in the Cherry+-infected cells at day 2 after Ngn3 delivery in acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: In Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion, we observed strong suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 at day 2 after Ngn3 delivery
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The pan-endocrine factor Pax6 was induced at day 2 in Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: The pan-endocrine factor Pax6 was also induced at day 2 (B).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The Mist1-Pax6+ state was maintained in the majority of Cherry+ cells at later time points in Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: The Mist1-Pax6+ state was maintained in the majority of Cherry+ cells at later time points (E, F, I, J).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7E,F,I,J.

claim: δ-subtype specific factors Sst and CCkbr were not induced until day 4 in Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: In contrast, δ-subtype specific factors Sst and CCkbr were not induced until day 4 (G, H)
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7G,H.

claim: δ-subtype specific factors Sst and CCkbr became robustly expressed at day 10 in Ngn3-induced acinar to δ-cell conversion.
source: and became robustly expressed at day 10 (K, L).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7K,L.

claim: Near complete suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 was observed in the Cherry+-infected cells at day 2 in M3-induced acinar to β-cell conversion.
source: In acinar to β-cell conversion induced by M3 (Ngn3+Mafa+Pdx1), near complete suppression of the acinar factor Mist1 was observed in the Cherry+-infected cells at day 2 (A).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The pan-endocrine factor Pax6 was robustly induced at day 2 in M3-induced acinar to β-cell conversion.
source: The pan-endocrine factor Pax6 was also robustly induced at day 2 (B).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: β-subtype specific factors insulin and Nkx6.1 were not induced until day 5 in M3-induced acinar to β-cell conversion.
source: In contrast, β-subtype specific factors insulin and Nkx6.1 were not induced until day 5 (G, H)
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8G,H.

claim: β-subtype specific factors insulin and Nkx6.1 became more robustly expressed at day 10 in M3-induced acinar to β-cell conversion.
source: and became more robustly expressed at day 10 (K, L).
evidence: This is based on time-course immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8K,L.

claim: Establishment of endocrine state precedes activation of endocrine subtype-specific genes in acinar conversion.
source: To further understand the temporal sequence of acinar to endocrine subtype conversion, we examined three key events: acinar suppression, pan-endocrine activation, and subtype-specific gene activation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the time-course data presented in Figures 7-8.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of Mafa with Ngn3 reduced the efficiency of somatostatin induction from 40 ± 3% to 11 ± 2%.
source: Polycistronic co-expression of Mafa with Ngn3 reduced the efficiency of somatostatin induction from 40 ± 3% in control Ngn3 animals
evidence: This is based on quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Polycistronic co-expression of Pdx1 with Ngn3 nearly completely suppressed somatostatin induction (1 ± 1%).
source: Polycistronic co-expression of Pdx1 and Ngn3 nearly completely suppressed Sst+ cell induction (C).
evidence: This is based on quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9C,D.

claim: The Sst-cherry+ cells expressed synaptophysin, suggesting that these cells acquired an endocrine identity but δ-specification was blocked.
source: The Sst-cherry+ cells expressed synaptophysin (Syn) (C, inset), suggesting that these cells acquired an endocrine identity but δ-specification was blocked.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 9C inset and is an inference about cell identity.

claim: Pdx1 and Mafa can suppress δ-subtype specification.
source: We tested the possibility that δ-specification may be suppressed by Pdx1 and/or Mafa.
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by the data in Figure 9 showing reduced somatostatin induction when Mafa or Pdx1 are co-expressed with Ngn3.

claim: Pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to endocrine δ- and α-like cells by in vivo expression of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
source: Our studies indicate that pancreatic acinar cells can be directly converted to endocrine δ- and α-like cells by in vivo expression of Ngn3 or Ngn3+Mafa respectively.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the main findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Acinar to endocrine reprogramming includes two main processes: establishment of a generic endocrine state and endocrine subtype specification.
source: Our studies indicate that acinar to endocrine reprogramming includes two main processes: establishment of a generic endocrine state and endocrine subtype specification (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a conceptual model based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Ngn3 plays a central role in promoting the endocrine state at the onset of reprogramming by suppressing acinar fate regulators and activating pan-endocrine genes.
source: Ngn3 plays a central role in promoting the endocrine state at the onset of reprogramming by suppressing acinar fate regulators and activating pan-endocrine genes (Figure 10B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in Figures 5-8.

claim: Continued expression of key acinar factors will block endocrine conversion.
source: This early step is critical as continued expression of key acinar factors will block endocrine conversion.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 6 showing that co-expression of acinar factors inhibits endocrine gene activation.

claim: Mafa suppresses acinar regulators but does not activate pan-endocrine genes.
source: Compared with Ngn3, Mafa suppresses acinar regulators but does not activate pan-endocrine genes
evidence: This is based on the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Pdx1 lacks the ability to suppress acinar regulators or activate pan-endocrine genes.
source: whereas Pdx1 lacks the ability to initiate either of these two events.
evidence: This is based on the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: The main function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to collaborate with Ngn3 to activate subtype-specific genes such as Arx in α-induction and Nkx6.1 in β-induction.
source: It is likely that the main function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to collaborate with Ngn3 to activate subtype-specific genes such as Arx in α-induction (this study) and Nkx6.1 in β-induction (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and cited work.

claim: Another important function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to suppress δ-specification, thus ensuring formation of singular α- and β-subtypes, and preventing hybrid cells.
source: Another important function of Mafa and Pdx1 is to suppress δ-specification, thus ensuring formation of singular α- and β-subtypes, and preventing hybrid cells (Figure 10B, lower panel).
evidence: This is based on the data in Figure 9 showing suppression of somatostatin induction by Mafa and Pdx1.

claim: Each of the three factors possesses both activator and suppressor functions.
source: Our data together suggest that each of the three factors possesses both activator and suppressor functions (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Ngn3 can suppress exocrine fate and promote endocrine fate during both embryogenesis in progenitor cells and during adulthood in differentiated acinar cells.
source: Thus, Ngn3 can suppress exocrine fate and promote endocrine fate during both embryogenesis in progenitor cells and during adulthood in differentiated acinar cells.
evidence: This is based on the current study's data and cited developmental studies.

claim: No genetic factors have been discovered that specify δ-cell fate in pancreas development.
source: Among the pancreatic endocrine subtypes, relatively little is known about the δ-cells. No genetic factors have been discovered that specify δ-cell fate in pancreas development.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The optimal method to induce Gcg+ α-like cells is by co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from two separate viruses at a 1:1 ratio.
source: The optimal method to induce Gcg+ α-like cells is by co-expression of Ngn3 and Mafa from two separate viruses at a 1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations comparing different delivery methods.

claim: Varying the ratio of the two viruses or polycistronic co-expression of both factors led to reduced α-cell formation.
source: Varying the ratio of the two viruses or polycistronic co-expression of both factors led to reduced α-cell formation.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The induction of α-like cells may require optimized Ngn3/Mafa stoichiometry along with other conditions such as specific expression level and dynamics of the factors.
source: We speculate that the induction of α-like cells may similarly require optimized Ngn3/Mafa stoichiometry along with other conditions such as specific expression level and dynamics of the factors
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations and comparison to iPS reprogramming.

claim: A suitable strategy to produce specific subtypes of cells by lineage conversion is to combine factors that confer broad competence with factors that confer subtype specificity.
source: Our studies suggest that a suitable strategy to produce specific subtypes of cells by lineage conversion is to combine factors that confer broad competence with factors that confer subtype specificity.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: β-cells secret insulin and play a key role in blood glucose regulation.
source: β-cells secret insulin and play a key role in blood glucose regulation
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-cell function.

claim: α- and δ-cells secrete glucagon and somatostatin to support β-cell function.
source: whereas α- and δ-cells secrete glucagon and somatostatin to support β-cell function (Edlund, 2001; Jensen, 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The most important gene that controls endogenous α-cell development and identity is the transcription factor Arx.
source: The most important gene that controls endogenous α-cell development and identity is the transcription factor Arx.
evidence: This is established knowledge about α-cell development.

claim: Genetic deletion of Arx during embryonic development results in the absence of α-cells.
source: Genetic deletion of Arx during embryonic development results in the absence of α-cells
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Ectopic expression of Arx in β-cells causes their phenotypic drift towards α-cells.
source: whereas ectopic expression of Arx in β-cells causes their phenotypic drift towards α-cells (Collombat et al., 2003; Dhawan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The secretory granules of each islet subtype have characteristic morphology.
source: In particular, the secretory granules of each islet subtype have characteristic morphology (Larsson et al., 1976; Leiter et al., 1979).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Insulin2 gene expression is regulated by DNA sequences located within approximately 400 bp upstream of the transcription start site.
source: Studies have shown that insulin2 gene expression is regulated by DNA sequences located within approximately 400 bp upstream of the transcription start site (TSS) (Hay and Docherty, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Approximately 200 bp of the Amylase 2 promoter is sufficient to direct acinar-specific expression.
source: Similarly, approximately 200 bp of the Amylase 2 promoter is sufficient to direct acinar-specific expression (Minami et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Not all cell fate conversion events are associated with DNA methylation changes.
